literal: " He Ruo hunched his shoulders and walked out.
idiomatic: " Xu He hunched his shoulders and walked out.

literal: Shun then shouted at him: "A mere clerk with brush and knife—fit only for a desk officer. How dare he hold a halberd here and shame our kinship!"
idiomatic: Shun shouted after him, "A brush-and-knife clerk, fit only for a desk—how dare he bear a halberd here and shame our kinship!"

literal: " He flung his robe and rose.
idiomatic: " He flung his robe aside and stood.

literal: The Empress Dowager was silent.
idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said nothing.

literal: At the time they were reviewing Shun's father's merit in the imperial entrustment; Prince of Rencheng Yi was given an additional fief of two thousand households, and five hundred of Yi's fief was split off to enfeoff Shun as Duke of Dong'a.
idiomatic: The court was then reviewing Shun's father's merit in the imperial entrustment; Prince of Rencheng Yi received two thousand additional households, and five hundred of Yi's fief was carved out to make Shun Duke of Dong'a.

literal: Shun, fearing that Hui and the others were undermining him, thereupon wrote "The Flies."
idiomatic: Fearing Hui and the others were undermining him, Shun wrote "The Flies."

literal: When illness kept him at home, he cut off all congratulations and condolences.
idiomatic: Illness kept him at home; he refused all congratulations and condolences.

literal: Later he was made Director of the Masters of Writing and Concurrent Right Vice Director, receiving office the same day as Prince of Chengyang Hui.
idiomatic: He was later made Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent right vice director, taking office the same day as Prince of Chengyang Hui.

literal: Gentleman-in-Attendance Zheng Yan first paid court to Hui outside the Halting Carriage Gate, then bowed to Shun.
idiomatic: Gentleman-in-Attendance Zheng Yan first paid court to Hui outside the Halting Carriage Gate, then bowed to Shun.

literal: Shun said in anger: "You are a flatterer—you should bow to a flatterer's prince.
idiomatic: Shun said in anger, "You are a flatterer—you should bow to a flatterer's prince.

literal: I am an upright man and do not accept a crooked bow."
idiomatic: I am an upright man and will not accept a crooked bow."

literal: Yan was deeply apologetic.
idiomatic: Yan apologized deeply.

literal: Shun said: "You are a son of a great house, yet you are a favorite of the Northern Palace; Vice Director Li Sichong still shares a scroll with Wang Luocheng—by that measure you too should follow on the next roll."
idiomatic: Shun said, "You are a son of a great house, yet a favorite of the Northern Palace; Vice Director Li Sichong still shares a scroll with Wang Luocheng—by that measure you belong on the next roll too."

literal: Those who saw it were shaken, while Shun remained perfectly at ease.
idiomatic: Onlookers were shaken; Shun remained perfectly at ease.

literal: When he went up to the Secretariat and climbed the steps toward the couch, he saw the couch was very old and asked the chief clerical officer Xu Wuqi.
idiomatic: Going up to the Secretariat and climbing toward the couch, he found it very old and asked the chief clerical officer Xu Wuqi.

literal: Wuqi said: "This couch once had the late emperor sit on it."
idiomatic: Wuqi said, "The late emperor once sat on this couch."

literal: Shun at once choked up; tears streamed down; for a long time he could not speak, and he ordered it replaced.
idiomatic: Shun choked up; tears streamed; long he could not speak, and he ordered it replaced.

literal: At the time the chief clerical officer of the Three Offices Cao, Zhu Hui, had long served Recording Director Prince of Gaoyang Yong; Yong wished to make him a reviewer of the Court of Justice and repeatedly pressed Shun, but Shun would not use him.
idiomatic: Zhu Hui, chief clerical officer of the Three Offices Cao, had long served Recording Director Prince of Gaoyang Yong; Yong wished to make him a Court of Justice reviewer and repeatedly pressed Shun, but Shun refused.

literal: Yong then issued an order to use him; Shun threw it to the ground.
idiomatic: Yong issued an order appointing him; Shun threw it to the floor.

literal: When Yong heard of it he was greatly angered; at dawn he sat in the metropolitan review hall, summoned the director and all the section chiefs to gather, intending to wait for Shun's arrival and humiliate him before the assembly.
idiomatic: Yong was furious; at dawn he sat in the metropolitan review hall and summoned the director and all section chiefs, intending to humble Shun before them when he arrived.

literal: Shun came only when the sun was high.
idiomatic: Shun arrived only when the sun stood high.

literal: Yong rolled up his sleeves, struck the table, and said: "I am the Son of Heaven's son, the Son of Heaven's younger brother, the Son of Heaven's uncle, the Son of Heaven's chief minister—within the four seas none is more honored.
idiomatic: Yong rolled up his sleeves, struck the table, and said, "I am the Son of Heaven's son, brother, uncle, and chief minister—within the four seas none stands higher.

literal: What sort of man is Yuan Shun, that he throws my written order to the ground!"
idiomatic: What sort of man is Yuan Shun, to throw my written order to the ground!"

literal: Shun's beard bristled; he looked up at the rafters; rage surged; he sighed long and said nothing.
idiomatic: Shun's beard bristled; he looked up at the rafters; rage surged; he sighed long and said nothing.

literal: After a long while he waved a white feather fan and said slowly to Yong: "The High Ancestor moved the capital to the central lands and fixed the nine ranks; official grades were set clear and dark, a model for ten thousand ages.
idiomatic: After a long while he waved a white feather fan and said slowly to Yong, "The High Ancestor moved the capital to the central lands and fixed the nine ranks; grades were set clear and dark, a model for ten thousand ages.

literal: Yet Zhu Hui is a petty man, a clerical officer of the Secretariat—how is he fit to be a clean official of the Court of Justice?
idiomatic: Yet Zhu Hui is a petty man, a Secretariat clerk—how is he fit for a clean post in the Court of Justice?

literal: Your Highness shares the late emperor's blood; you truly ought to follow the edict and keep to the constant rule—why overstep it again?"
idiomatic: Your Highness shares the late emperor's blood; you ought to follow the edict and keep to the constant rule—why overstep it again?"

literal: Yong said: "As chief minister and recording director, how may I not appoint one man to office?"
idiomatic: Yong said, "As chief minister and recording director, how may I not appoint one man to office?"

literal: Shun said: "Though the cook does not manage the kitchen, the corpse-blesser does not step past the wine-vessel and stand in for him.
idiomatic: Shun said, "Though the cook does not manage the kitchen, the corpse-blesser does not step past the wine-vessel and stand in for him.

literal: I have not heard of any separate edict ordering Your Highness to participate in selections."
idiomatic: I have not heard of any separate edict ordering Your Highness to participate in selections."

literal: Shun again said sharply: "If Your Highness insists, Shun will memorialize the matter to the throne."
idiomatic: Shun said sharply again, "If Your Highness insists, Shun will memorialize the matter to the throne."

literal: Yong then laughed and said: "How can one grow angry over a petty man like Zhu Hui."
idiomatic: Yong laughed and said, "How can one grow angry over a petty man like Zhu Hui."

literal: He rose, called Shun into the inner room, and drank with him to the utmost.
idiomatic: He rose, called Shun into the inner room, and drank with him to the utmost.

literal: Shun's lofty firmness and refusal to bend were all of this kind.
idiomatic: Shun's lofty firmness and refusal to bend were all of this kind.

literal: Later he was made Concurrent Left Vice Director.
idiomatic: He was later made concurrent left vice director.

literal: When Erzhu Rong received Emperor Zhuangdi, he summoned all the hundred officials to Heyin.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong received Emperor Zhuangdi, he summoned all the hundred officials to Heyin.

literal: He had long heard that Shun often remonstrated; he prized his bright integrity and told Zhu Rui: "Tell Vice Director Yuan to stay at the Secretariat—he need not come."
idiomatic: He had long heard Shun often remonstrated; he prized his bright integrity and told Zhu Rui, "Tell Vice Director Yuan to stay at the Secretariat—he need not come."

literal: Shun did not grasp his meaning; hearing that the officials were to be harmed, he fled at once and was killed by tomb-guard Xianyu Kangnu.
idiomatic: Shun did not grasp his meaning; hearing that the officials were to be harmed, he fled and was killed by tomb-guard Xianyu Kangnu.

literal: His house had bare walls and no goods to store—only several thousand volumes of books.
idiomatic: His house had bare walls and nothing to store—only several thousand volumes of books.

literal: Gentleman-in-Attendance Wang Caida tore his robe to cover him.
idiomatic: Gentleman-in-Attendance Wang Caida tore his robe to cover him.

literal: When Emperor Zhuangdi returned to the palace, he sent Yellow Gate Attendant Shan Wei to tour and announce the capital.
idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangdi returned to the palace, he sent Yellow Gate Attendant Shan Wei to tour the capital and announce the restoration.

literal: Wei came to Shun's mourning hall and wept without end.
idiomatic: Wei came to Shun's mourning hall and wept without end.

literal: When he returned, Emperor Zhuangdi wondered at his broken voice; Wei reported the circumstances.
idiomatic: On his return the emperor wondered at his broken voice; Wei reported what he had seen.

literal: Emperor Zhuangdi ordered Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Zhi: "The imperial clan has not suffered one death alone—it cannot all be compensated.
idiomatic: The emperor ordered Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Zhi, "The imperial clan has lost more than one man—it cannot all be compensated.

literal: Vice Director Yuan's integrity in poverty shines brighter in death; grant him a special gift of a hundred bolts of silk—let no other case follow this."
idiomatic: Vice Director Yuan's integrity in poverty shines brighter in death; grant a special gift of a hundred bolts of silk—let no other case follow."

literal: He was posthumously made Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of the Secretariat; his posthumous title was Wenlie.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of the Secretariat, posthumous title Wenlie.

literal: Earlier, when the emperor was still in his princedom, Shun dreamed that a stretch of black cloud came straight from the northwest, struck the sun and moon in the southeast and broke them both, then veiled all the stars; heaven and earth were wholly dark.
idiomatic: Earlier, while the emperor was still in his princedom, Shun dreamed a stretch of black cloud came straight from the northwest, struck the sun and moon in the southeast and broke them, veiled all the stars, and left heaven and earth wholly dark.

literal: Soon the cloud and mist dispersed, and the sun came out from the southwest corner, very bright and clear; the cloud was long, the Prince of Changle's sun.
idiomatic: Soon cloud and mist dispersed; the sun came out from the southwest corner, bright and clear—the cloud was long, the Prince of Changle's sun.

literal: Presently he saw Emperor Zhuangdi enter from the Changhe Gate, ascend the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and three times the cry of "ten thousand years" went up; the hundred officials all put on court dress to attend the emperor, while Shun alone, in the western corridor of the Secretariat by the locust tree, removed cap and robe and lay down.
idiomatic: Presently he saw Emperor Zhuangdi enter from Changhe Gate, ascend the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and "ten thousand years" ring out three times; officials all donned court dress to attend, while Shun alone in the Secretariat's western corridor by the locust tree removed cap and robe and lay down.

literal: When he woke he told Yuan Huiye: "My dream last night was very bad for me."
idiomatic: When he woke he told Yuan Huiye, "My dream last night was very bad for me."

literal: He told the dream and interpreted it: "Black cloud is the color of ill qi, the color of the north—there will surely be a northern enemy who will disorder the capital, harm the two palaces, and ruin the hundred officials.
idiomatic: He told the dream and interpreted it: "Black cloud is ill qi, the color of the north—a northern enemy will surely disorder the capital, harm the two palaces, and ruin the hundred officials.

literal: How so?
idiomatic: How so?

literal: The sun is the image of the ruler.
idiomatic: The sun is the image of the ruler.

literal: The moon is the image of the empress.
idiomatic: The moon is the image of the empress.

literal: The host of stars are the image of the hundred officials.
idiomatic: The host of stars are the image of the hundred officials.

literal: By this reasoning, will not the capital suffer calamity?
idiomatic: By this reasoning, will not the capital suffer calamity?

literal: Formerly Liu Yao destroyed the Jin house and made a platform of skulls—will not what lies ahead be like this?
idiomatic: Formerly Liu Yao destroyed the Jin house and made a platform of skulls—will not what lies ahead be like this?

literal: Even so, Prince of Pengcheng Xie had civil virtue throughout the realm; now the dream shows his son as Son of Heaven—accumulated virtue must be rewarded; this is certain!
idiomatic: Even so, Prince of Pengcheng Xie had civil virtue throughout the realm; now the dream shows his son as Son of Heaven—accumulated virtue must be rewarded; this is certain.

literal: I only regret that he will not hold it long.
idiomatic: I only regret he will not hold it long.

literal: The reason is that he comes from the southwest; by the season changing the year, it will not exceed three years.
idiomatic: The reason is he comes from the southwest; by season changing year, it will not exceed three years.

literal: I only regret that I will not see it.
idiomatic: I only regret I will not see it.

literal: How so?
idiomatic: How so?

literal: I dreamed I lay under a locust tree; the character for locust has 'tree' beside 'ghost'—my person and a ghost together; again I removed cap and robe—will this not mean death?
idiomatic: I dreamed I lay under a locust tree; locust has 'tree' beside 'ghost'—my person and a ghost together; again I removed cap and robe—will this not mean death?

literal: Yet after death I shall receive the three dukes' posthumous gift."
idiomatic: Yet after death I shall receive the three dukes' posthumous gift."

literal: All came about as in the dream.
idiomatic: All came about as in the dream.

literal: Shun compiled "Records of Emperors" in twenty scrolls, and several tens of poems, rhapsodies, memorials, and eulogies—most are now lost.
idiomatic: Shun compiled Records of Emperors in twenty scrolls and several tens of poems, rhapsodies, memorials, and eulogies—most are now lost.

literal: His eldest son Lang, then seventeen, lay with a blade in hiding for many years, then with his own hand cut down Kangnu and offered the head at Shun's tomb, then went to the palace gate to confess his crime.
idiomatic: His eldest son Lang, then seventeen, lay with a blade in hiding for years, then with his own hand cut down Kangnu and offered the head at Shun's tomb, then went to the palace gate to confess.

literal: The court praised him and did not punish him.
idiomatic: The court praised him and did not punish him.

literal: Lang held the office of Secretariat Attendant.
idiomatic: Lang held the office of Secretariat Attendant.

literal: In the Tianping era he was killed by a slave; posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: In the Tianping era he was killed by a slave and was posthumously made right vice director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Shun's younger brother Ji, courtesy name Zigang, followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong and held Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Prince of Huashan.
idiomatic: Shun's younger brother Ji, courtesy name Zigang, followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong and held left vice director of the Masters of Writing and the title Prince of Huashan.

literal: Prince of Nan'an Zhen was enfeoffed in the second year of Huangxing.
idiomatic: Prince of Nan'an Zhen was enfeoffed in the second year of Huangxing.

literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was repeatedly promoted to Grand General of the Chang'an Garrison and Governor of Yong Province.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen he rose to Grand General of the Chang'an Garrison and Governor of Yong.

literal: Zhen by nature was loyal and careful.
idiomatic: Zhen was loyal and careful by nature.

literal: When his mother's illness was grave, his grief and emaciation were extraordinary; then a white pheasant wandered before his courtyard.
idiomatic: When his mother's illness grew grave, his grief and emaciation were extraordinary; then a white pheasant wandered in his courtyard.

literal: The emperor heard of his moving heaven and earth and gave a thousand bolts of silk to praise and honor him.
idiomatic: The emperor heard how he had moved heaven and earth and gave a thousand bolts of silk in praise.

literal: Summoned to lecture on military affairs and received audience in the Hall of Imperial Trust, he was admonished: "Your filial conduct shows in your private hall and your fair name shines in the realm; as a close kin of the state you will never know poverty or low station.
idiomatic: Summoned to lecture on military affairs and received in the Hall of Imperial Trust, he was admonished: "Your filial conduct shows at home and your fair name in the realm; as close kin of the state you will never know poverty.

literal: What you should beware of is roughly three things: first, relying on kinship and acting arrogant, violating ritual and overstepping measure;
idiomatic: What you should beware of is roughly three things: first, relying on kinship, acting arrogant, violating ritual and overstepping measure;

literal: second, arrogance, greed, and luxury, not caring for government;
idiomatic: second, arrogance, greed, and luxury, not caring for government;

literal: third, drinking wine, roaming in pleasure, and not choosing whom you befriend.
idiomatic: third, drinking, roaming in pleasure, and not choosing whom you befriend.

literal: If you do not cast off these three, disaster and calamity will be born."
idiomatic: Cast off none of these three and disaster will be born."

literal: Zhen could not follow and obey; afterward he gathered wealth and indulged his desires.
idiomatic: Zhen could not follow and obey; afterward he gathered wealth and indulged his desires.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen, because Zhen's filial nurture was famed within and without, especially pardoned him, stripped his enfeoffment, sent him home as a commoner, and confined him for life.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen, because Zhen's filial nurture was famed within and without, especially pardoned him, stripped his enfeoffment, sent him home as a commoner, and confined him for life.

literal: Because he took part in deciding the move of the capital, he was again enfeoffed Prince of Nan'an, made Grand General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Xiang Province.
idiomatic: Because he took part in deciding the move of the capital, he was again enfeoffed Prince of Nan'an, made Grand General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Xiang.

literal: The emperor saw Zhen off at the Hualin Metropolitan Pavilion and ordered all to compose poems.
idiomatic: The emperor saw Zhen off at the Hualin Metropolitan Pavilion and ordered all to compose poems.

literal: Those who could not might still be allowed to shoot arrows—warriors would bend the bow, men of letters take up the brush.
idiomatic: Those who could not might still shoot arrows—warriors would bend the bow, men of letters take up the brush.

literal: The emperor escorted Zhen down the steps, parting with tears.
idiomatic: The emperor escorted Zhen down the steps, parting in tears.

literal: In the fifth month of the twentieth year of Taihe he reached Ye.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twentieth year of Taihe he reached Ye.

literal: On the day of the imperial birthday, violent wind and rain struck; several tens froze to death.
idiomatic: On the day of the imperial birthday, violent wind and rain struck; several tens froze to death.

literal: Zhen again, because of drought, prayed for rain to the host of spirits.
idiomatic: Zhen again, because of drought, prayed for rain to the host of spirits.

literal: In Ye city was the temple of Shi Jilong; the people worshipped it.
idiomatic: In Ye stood the temple of Shi Jilong; the people worshipped it.

literal: Zhen told the spirit-image: "If in three days there is no rain, I will add the whip's punishment."
idiomatic: Zhen told the spirit-image, "If in three days there is no rain, I will add the whip's punishment."

literal: The prayer for rain did not succeed; he then whipped the image a hundred strokes.
idiomatic: The prayer for rain failed; he whipped the image a hundred strokes.

literal: That month a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died; his posthumous title was Hui.
idiomatic: That month a carbuncle broke on his back and he died; posthumous title Hui.

literal: When Governor of Heng Province Mu Tai plotted rebellion, Zhen knew and did not report it.
idiomatic: When Governor of Heng Mu Tai plotted rebellion, Zhen knew and did not report it.

literal: Though dead, his rank and fief were still stripped posthumously and the state abolished.
idiomatic: Though dead, his rank and fief were still stripped posthumously and the state abolished.

literal: His son Ying by nature was clever and keen, skilled at riding and shooting, understood music, and knew a little medicine.
idiomatic: His son Ying was clever and keen by nature, skilled at riding and shooting, understood music, and knew a little medicine.

literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was Governor of Liang Province.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was Governor of Liang.

literal: When the emperor campaigned south he was Separate Route Commander-in-Chief of Hanzhong.
idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned south he was separate-route commander-in-chief of Hanzhong.

literal: Later, when the great host reached Zhongli, Ying because the imperial carriage moved in person and momentum tilted toward the southeast, and Hanzhong had an opening to exploit, memorialized asking to pursue and strike; the emperor approved.
idiomatic: Later, when the great host reached Zhongli, Ying—seeing the emperor move in person, momentum tilt southeast, and Hanzhong open to exploit—memorialized asking to pursue and strike; the emperor approved.
